:::{#exm-measurable-function}
#### Measurable and not measurable

On the die rolls $D$, take the $\sigma$-algebra
$\mathscr{S} = \set{\emptyset, \set{2, 4, 6}, \set{1, 3, 5}, D}$
of @exm-sigma-algebra.

- Let $f(x) = 1$ for even $x$ and $f(x) = 0$ for odd $x$.
  The set $\set{x \in D : f(x) \le c}$ is
  $\emptyset$ when $c < 0$,
  $\set{1, 3, 5}$ when $0 \le c < 1$,
  and $D$ when $c \ge 1$.
  All three are in $\mathscr{S}$, so $f$ is measurable.
- Let $g(x) = x$.
  Then $\set{x \in D : g(x) \le 1} = \set{1}$,
  which is not in $\mathscr{S}$, so $g$ is not measurable.

With the $\sigma$-algebra of all subsets of $D$ instead,
every set $\set{x \in D : g(x) \le c}$ is a subset of $D$,
so every function $D \to \reals$, including $g$, is measurable.

:::
